creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The laptop daemon reads the next request on a connection only after it has answered the one before. `serve` in `crates/muster-daemon/src/control.rs` handles a message request inline (line 239), and a carried one waits there up to a minute (`CARRYING`) for the machine that keeps the group. Everything else the window asks the laptop daemon on that connection, pane requests included, waits behind it.

On the owner's laptop (0.19.0, 2026-10-27), the window's msg.group_delete for a group kept on devenv waited 46.7 s on connection 3. Three `msg.log` fetches the window sent behind it, to show that group's conversation (ids 351-353), each timed out after 10 s and logged `conversation.fetch_failed`, so the conversation showed a spinner and no messages. All of them were answered at 22:45:24.429 UTC, the fetches in 0.2 ms each. Run log: `~/Library/Logs/muster/muster-2026-10-26_09-03-57-35622.jsonl`.

The daemon's own log hides the wait. `received` is taken after the request is read off the socket (line 216), so the fetches' `daemon.request.answered` lines say `ms` 0.2 and `queued_ms` 0.1 for requests that sat unread for up to 37 s.

Restarts already avoid this: `Handled::Restart` is answered off the connection's thread (line 281), because an answer carries its request's id and may follow later ones. A carried message request could be answered the same way.
title: A carried message request holds up every later request on the window's connection to its daemon
